variants: Reachy Mini Wireless, which carries its own computer and battery, and Reachy Mini Lite, which runs from the buyer's Mac, PC or Linux machine. Pollen sells Reachy 2 separately, which this record does not cover.
availability_note: Pollen Robotics' Reachy Mini page has Order Now buttons for the Wireless and Lite kits that open its store, offers its distributor Seeed Studio outside the EU, UK, US and Canada, states prices, and says the lead time is up to 90 days after purchase. Both versions ship as DIY kits.

hardware.compute: A Raspberry Pi 4 Compute Module (CM4104016 with Wi-Fi, 4 GB of RAM and 16 GB of flash) in the Wireless version. The Lite version uses the buyer's computer.
hardware.sensors: A wide-angle 12 MP autofocus camera, a four-microphone array and a speaker, with an accelerometer on the Wireless version.
hardware.actuation: Dynamixel motors driving 6 degrees of freedom in the head, 1 rotation of the body and 1 rotation of each of the two antennas, in a body of 30 x 20 x 15.5 cm extended and 1.475 kg.
hardware.power: A 6.8 to 7.6 V input and, in the Wireless version, a LiFePO4 2000 mAh, 6.4 V, 12.8 Wh battery. The Lite version is powered from a wall outlet.

developer_access: Pollen's integration guide opens "Reachy Mini is designed for AI Builders. Here is how to integrate LLMs and share your work." and says "The Daemon exposes full control via REST." Its AI-integration guide describes the architecture as "LLM decides → Tool call (e.g., "dance") → Queue move → Control loop executes smoothly", says "The LLM doesn't control motors directly", and lists the tools the reference app gives the LLM: move_head, dance, play_emotion, camera and head_tracking. The reference reachy_mini_conversation_app repository describes itself as a "Conversational app for the Reachy Mini robot combining realtime voice, vision, personality-aware tools, and choreographed motion." Pollen's page says the robot's built-in conversation is "Powered by a realtime voice model" without naming one.
